# Sysctl

Kernel parameters, written to sysctl.d files and applied.

## Where it is served

| Surface | Where |
| ------- | ----- |
| API | `/api/node/{hostname}/sysctl`, in [API](/category/api) |
| CLI | `osapi client node sysctl` |
| Jobs | `behavior.sysctl.<method>`, run by the agent |

## Built on

| Uses | Used by |
| ---- | ------- |
| [managedfile](../managedfile/managedfile.md) | Nothing |

## Where it runs

On `debian`. On any other platform its methods report `skipped`.

It runs `sysctl` with sudo, so the agent's user needs a sudoers entry for it
unless the agent runs as root. `osapi agent start` checks this at startup.

It writes `/etc/sysctl.d/osapi-*.conf`.

In a trace, a call is the span `behavior.sysctl.<method>`, with `behavior.managedfile.<method>`, `exec sysctl`, `exec chown`, `exec stat`, `file.write`, `file.remove`, `file.chmod`, `kv.get`, `kv.put` under it.

Its span records the input `key` (get, create, update, delete).

## Methods

| Method | Verb | Permission | Description |
| ------ | ---- | ---------- | ----------- |
| [`list`](../../usage/cli/client/node/sysctl/list.md) | read | `sysctl:read` | List the kernel's parameters and which osapi manages |
| [`get`](../../usage/cli/client/node/sysctl/get.md) | read | `sysctl:read` | Get a kernel parameter's current value, and whether osapi manages it |
| [`create`](../../usage/cli/client/node/sysctl/create.md) | write | `sysctl:write` | Manage a kernel parameter and apply it |
| [`update`](../../usage/cli/client/node/sysctl/update.md) | write | `sysctl:write` | Set a kernel parameter, manage it, and apply it |
| [`delete`](../../usage/cli/client/node/sysctl/delete.md) | write | `sysctl:write` | Stop the management of a kernel parameter |

## Settings

Read by the agent, under `behaviors.sysctl` in the config. Each can also be set
with its environment variable or its `osapi agent start` flag.

| Key | Flag | Environment | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | ---- | ----------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `behaviors.sysctl.dir` | `--sysctl-dir` | `OSAPI_BEHAVIORS_SYSCTL_DIR` | string | `/etc/sysctl.d` | Directory the agent writes osapi's kernel parameter files to, one osapi-&lt;key&gt;.conf per key. |

## Inspecting it

```bash
osapi behavior get --name sysctl                           # surfaces, methods, types, settings, telemetry
osapi behavior method get --name sysctl --method <method>  # one method, with its JSON Schema
```
